deviations.text: UN Regulations were read from their EUR-Lex OJ publications (unece.org returned HTTP 403), as in L1. Each was located by a SPARQL title query on the EU Publications Office endpoint; amendment, supplement and corrigendum titles were filtered out by script before printing, and the most recent remaining full-text OJ publication (sector 4) was chosen by document date without displaying the other publications. Hit counts of matching full-text publications are recorded. Two first-pass picks were non-UN EU acts with the same number (Regulation No 1 on languages; Regulation No 31 Staff Regulations) and consolidated-text CELEX numbers (sector 0) for R38/R77/R87/R91; the query was re-run restricted to sector-4 UN publications and those picks replaced. No consolidated text was opened.

Regulation (EC) No 661/2009: references were taken from the OJ text as adopted (CELEX 32009R0661). Its Annex IV (list of UNECE Regulations) is empty in that text, so 661/2009 contributes no UN-Regulation references; a consolidated version was not used, because choosing one would require the version list. The UN Regulations relevant to lighting are reached through 2019/2144 Annex I and the UN seeds.

S1: the legal-basis SPARQL query (cdm:resource_legal_based_on_resource_legal) also returns European Parliament resolutions, a Commission report and Commission proposals (CELEX sectors 5). These are not acts adopted under the base act and are not kept even where the title test passes: 52010PC0310 (proposal for a Council Decision on compulsory application of UN Regulations including Nos 37, 48, 99 and 123) passes the title test but is not kept. A cross-check title query (titles containing the base-act number, sector 3) found no further act adopted under either base act. Adoption dates were stripped from the S1 titles by script.

SAE seeds L20-L22: the sae.org and SAE Mobilus pages are rendered client-side and load an AWS WAF captcha SDK; the static HTML holds no title or scope. Not bypassed. Exact titles: J578 is taken from 49 CFR 571.5 (an official incorporation list); J3069 and J1383 are the titles shown in web-search result titles for the SAE pages. Scope and references: not accessible.

Tests for SAE documents cited by FMVSS 108 (J567, J573, J602, J2009): the cited document's scope was not accessible, and its title (from 49 CFR 571.5) does not name road vehicles, so test 2 is recorded 'not established' and nothing is added. Read on title alone with the SAE ground-vehicle context, J602 (headlamp aiming device) and J2009 (discharge forward lighting systems) would pass all three tests. They are listed here for the reviewer as a sensitivity set and are NOT on the list. The same rule leaves UN R70 and UN R88 (cited by R48; no EUR-Lex OJ publication found; unece.org 403) not added.

Titles of some cited documents that fail test 1 or test 2 (ISO, IEC 60061/60410, ASTM, R24, R33) are recorded from the screener's knowledge, not from a landing page (iso.org returned 403 / bot challenge). None of these could change an addition except if the title were wrong in a way that names road vehicles and lighting; none is a lighting-on-vehicles title.

Disclosure (rule 1): two web searches were used to find landing URLs (IEC 60809 and IEC 60061 on webstore.iec.ch; SAE J3069/J1383/J578 on sae.org). The search tool returned, unrequested, a synthesized summary that mentioned edition and amendment information for IEC 60809, IEC 60061, SAE J1383 and SAE J3069. Nothing from those summaries is used in or recorded in these outputs, and no further web search was made. Separately, the std.samr.gov.cn search JSON rows and the GB detail page include edition-state fields; only the current (or, where none is current, the single most recent) edition's identifier was printed, except that one withdrawn-edition row of GB 4785 was seen in a raw response preview at the start of the GB search. The reviewer should weigh whether this exposure matters for the blind list; the list itself was fixed by the protocol, not by that information.

GB seeds GB 25991, GB 23255 and GB 17509 have no edition marked current on std.samr.gov.cn. The most recent edition's identifier is listed (only that row was printed). The current-state flag is recorded in the JSON for access purposes and carries no description of what changed.

Reference extraction for UN Regulations and EU acts is by script (identifier + clause), starting at the Scope heading (UN) or Article 1 (EU), and excluding sections headed 'Transitional provisions' and any bibliography. Approval-mark examples in annexes (e.g. R48 Annex 2 citing R33) are counted as citations because they are annex text. For 2019/2144 Annex I, a bare number in the 'UN Regulation Number' column was read as a citation of that UN Regulation with its subject; the series-of-amendments and OJ-reference columns were not read or printed.
